label: Cinematic
description: Film-language storytelling led by viewpoint, performance, dramatic information, sound, and motivated rhythm; not an automatic slow-motion filter.
intent: Protect genuine dramatic meaning and the audience viewpoint. The cut should advance feeling, information or perception; tempo can be fast, still or contrasting.
avoid: bright outlined words over emotionally quiet footage
mechanically long shots mistaken for cinema
forced teal/orange grading or fake film grain as proof of taste
reaction shots sourced from the wrong moment
covering dramatic silence with generic stock score
opening: Introduce a visual/sound situation, character need or dramatic question through genuine footage; withhold or reveal information only when the narrative warrants it.
editing: Emotion and performance > story meaning > rhythm > eye guidance > spatial continuity when tradeoffs arise. Preserve emotional transitions, establish cause/effect and geography when needed, use subjective POV/reaction only with truthful context. No mandated shot length or obligatory transition.
typography: Minimal motivated titles and credits; sparse readable lower thirds when needed, never assume cinema means letterbox bars or an arbitrary expensive-looking font.
sound: Use room tone, diegetic perspective, scene-specific textures, selective score and intentional silence. Consider J/L audio bridges only when authentic source handles exist and rights are clear.
critique: Does the scene convey whose perspective matters? Is the emotional transition continuous? Does the audience understand cause/effect and the sonic world? Would a sustained shot or meaningful contrast beat another cut?

creative_contrast.when: A new idea, action or visual fact arrives
The viewer needs to read, understand or feel something
